name: How are molding repairs handled in older or historic Denver area homes?

mainEntity.name: How are molding repairs handled in older or historic Denver area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Denver and Englewood homes built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, trim was often custom-milled in regional species and features taller, thicker profiles than modern dimensional lumber. Many historic homes also have plaster walls that are thicker and less uniform than modern drywall, which affects how trim sits against the wall. Replacing historic trim requires careful deconstruction to preserve surrounding plaster, followed by sourcing period-accurate profiles or building up composite trim layers to match original architectural details.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older local homes often feature non-standard lumber dimensions and plaster walls, requiring custom milling, layered trim buildups, and careful work to avoid damaging wall plaster.
